::: {#rem-rarity-ranges}
#### Values of the probability, the rarity and the surprisal

For a
[discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
the mass $\P(X=x)$ of an
[outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-experiment-outcome)
with a mass above $0$, its [rarity](#def-rarity) $\rarityf{x}$ and its [surprisal](#def-surprisal) $\surprisalf{x}$ take the values in the middle column.
For a
[continuous random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-continuous-rv),
the [density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) $\p(x)$ takes the place of the mass.
At a value $x$ with a density above $0$,
the rarity $\rarityf{x}$ is the reciprocal of $\p(x)$,
and the surprisal $\surprisalf{x}$ is the
[surprisal of a continuous value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-surprisal-continuous).
Their values are in the right column.

| | Mass $\P(X=x)$ | Density $\p(x)$ |
|---|---|---|
| Mass or density | $(0, 1]$ | $(0, \infty)$ |
| Rarity $\rarityf{x}$ | $[1, \infty)$ | $(0, \infty)$ |
| Surprisal $\surprisalf{x}$ | $[0, \infty)$ | $(-\infty, \infty)$ |

- **Mass.**
  A mass of $1$ gives the smallest rarity, $1$, and the smallest surprisal, $0$.
  No mass exceeds $1$, the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) of a certain outcome.
  So no mass gives a rarity below $1$ or a surprisal below $0$.
- **Density.**
  A density can be arbitrarily large, as in the
  [uniform example](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#exm-entropy-uniform),
  so the rarity can fall below $1$ and the surprisal can fall below $0$.
- **Zero.**
  A mass or density of $0$ gives a rarity and a surprisal of $\infty$.
- **Units.**
  A mass has no units.
  A density has the units of $1/x$,
  so its rarity has the units of $x$.
  Rescaling $x$ by a nonzero $c$ shifts its surprisal by $\logf{\abs{c}}$.

:::
